title: tasks-types `min_date_time`/`max_date_time` are `String` while calendars-types siblings are `UTCDate` — same RFC field, different Rust type
description:
**Files**:
- crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/capability.rs:49 — \`pub min_date_time: UTCDate\`
- crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/capability.rs:53 — \`pub max_date_time: UTCDate\`
- crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/capability.rs:52 — \`pub min_date_time: String\`
- crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/capability.rs:55 — \`pub max_date_time: String\`

**Divergence**: \`CalendarsAccountCapability\` and \`TasksAccountCapability\` both expose \`minDateTime\` and \`maxDateTime\` on the wire (per draft-ietf-jmap-calendars and draft-ietf-jmap-tasks). The two sibling type crates model the same wire shape with different Rust types:
- calendars uses the workspace newtype \`jmap_types::UTCDate\` (presumably wrapping a parsed/validated ISO 8601 datetime)
- tasks uses bare \`String\`

**What goes wrong**:
1. A consumer porting code between tasks and calendars must convert between \`String\` and \`UTCDate\` — \`UTCDate::parse(&task_cap.min_date_time)?\` on one side and \`cal_cap.min_date_time.to_string()\` on the other. No semantic reason for the asymmetry.
2. tasks loses the type-safety the workspace already paid for: \`UTCDate\` validates on parse; \`String\` accepts \`"not a date"\`.
3. Future extensions modelling datetime caps (e.g. a future scheduling extension) don't know which precedent to copy.

**Fix**: tasks-types should change \`min_date_time\` and \`max_date_time\` from \`String\` to \`UTCDate\`. This is a breaking change for any direct consumer of \`TasksAccountCapability\` (likely zero today — the crate is at v0.1.1 pre-release). The serde wire format is unchanged if \`UTCDate\` serializes as a string per workspace convention.

**Related**: tasks-types also exposes \`TasksRecurrencesAccountCapability.max_expanded_query_duration: String\` — this one is RFC 3339 duration (e.g. \`PT5M\`), not a datetime, so \`String\` is correct (no workspace newtype for ISO 8601 durations exists). Calendars-types uses the same \`String\` for its analogous \`max_expanded_query_duration\` — that one is consistent.
close_reason: Landed on main as e6f2687f (fix(tasks-types)!: type date caps as LocalDateTime; draft-tasks-06 1.6.1 LocalDate, not UTCDate). Review passed; integration CI green at 9e113188.
